criteria.criterion: A test run with `cargo test` drives the wrapper with one slot and two producer processes. The second blocks while the first holds the slot, then runs after the first finishes. Afterwards the slot is free (try_acquire succeeds).
criteria.evidence: the_second_producer_waits_for_the_one_slot_then_runs passed. It starts two real wrapper processes (a symlink to the athena binary) against a fake cargo and one slot. It checks that the second is queued (waiting()==1) and has not started. The log order is start a, end a, start b, end b. Afterwards take_soon() gets the slot through try_acquire.

criteria.criterion: A test runs `cargo -q build` and `cargo --locked test` through the wrapper against a fake cargo. It asserts that both took a slot while running and freed it afterwards. It fails if the wrapper reads only its first argument, so the test must break if the subcommand lookup is replaced with args[0].
criteria.evidence: a_global_flag_before_the_subcommand_does_not_skip_the_queue passed. For both forms it asserts slot_is_held() while the fake cargo runs, then take_soon() after it ends. With an args[0] lookup the subcommand would be "-q" or "--locked", which is not in SLOTTED, so no slot would be taken and the slot_is_held assertion would fail. I judged this from the code; I did not mutate it.

criteria.criterion: A test where no slot frees within the wait limit asserts that the command ends with the documented message ('no build slot free for ... s; try again') and a non-failure environment exit, and that the job is recorded as held (`environment: build slot wait`), not failed. summary: The wrapper does what the request asks. A `cargo` link to the athena binary goes first on the producer's PATH only. It finds the subcommand after the global flags using the policy's own CARGO_GLOBAL_FLAGS list, now made public, so there is no second copy. It holds a producer-class slot while build, test, clippy or check runs. Other subcommands, such as fmt and metadata, run without a slot. When no slot frees in time, it exits 75 with the documented message and writes a hold marker, and the run turns that marker into a held job. I ran the new integration tests (5), wrapper unit tests (4), env test, run-level hold test and policy tests; all pass. The verdict is still fail, because `cargo test` does not pass.
